PASSED IN M.V.C. NO.320/2009 ON THE FILE OF THE SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE & M.A.C.T., AT GANGAVATHI, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION IN THE INTEREST OF JUSTICE AND EQUITY.
 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
Challenging judgment and award dated 30.04.2011 passed by learned Senior Civil Judge and M.A.C.T, Gangavathi, in MVC No.320/2009, this appeal is filed by claimant for enhancement of compensation.

2. Brief facts as stated are that on 15.09.2009, when claimant was proceeding on motorcycle bearing registration no.KA-26/H-4722 from Gangavathi to Kampli, driver of lorry bearing no.AP-29/U-1982 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner dashed against motorcycle causing grievous injuries to claimant.
He was admitted to hospital.
Despite taking treatment, he did not recover fully.
3. Claiming compensation, he filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act against driver, owner and insurer of lorry.
4. On service of notice, driver of lorry entered appearance but, did not file objections.
Owner and insurer remained exparte.
5. Thereafter, tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence of claimant as PW1 and Dr.Balasubramanyam as PW2.
Exhibits P1 to P11 were got marked.
No rebuttal evidence was led.

sentences.text: On consideration, tribunal held that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of lorry by its driver, claimant was entitled for compensation assessed by it at Rs.86,800/-.

However, on ground that Ex.P6-notarized copy of driving licence of driver of insured vehicle was not in respect of heavy goods vehicle and respondent no.1-driver was holding licence to drive light motor vehicle,
tribunal dismissed claim petition against insurer and passed award against driver and owner.
7. Aggrieved by same, claimant is in appeal.

8. Shri B.Sharanabasawa, learned counsel appearing for claimant-appellant submits that,
admittedly, claimant was a third party in accident in question and offending vehicle was duly insured.
Even though driver of lorry did not possess driving licence to drive heavy goods vehicle, but he had licence to drive light motor vehicle.
Therefore, submitted that occurrence of accident was not solely on ground of driver not possessing valid and effective driving licence to drive that particular class of vehicle.
It was further submitted that this was a fit case, wherein order of pay and recovery ought to be made.

9. Insofar as quantum of compensation, it was submitted that even though claimant sustained fracture of patella and PW2 had assessed disability at 10% to 12% to whole body, but tribunal erred in taking it only at 10%.
It was further submitted that tribunal erred in taking meager amount of monthly income.
Even award under other heads was on lower side and sought enhancement.
10. On other hand, Shri S.S.Gundi, learned counsel for respondent no.3-insurer sought to support award and opposed enhancement.

It was firstly submitted that non-possession of driving licence to drive that particular class of vehicle would be a fundamental breach of terms and conditions of policy and therefore, insurer would not be held liable.
It is further submitted that claimant failed to produce any specific evidence to justify claim for enhancement on ground of higher income.
On over all consideration for fracture of patella, award appears to be just and proper and opposed enhancement.

11. Heard learned counsel for both parties and perused impugned judgment and award and record.
12.
From above submission, it is seen that claim petition is dismissed against insurer.
Claimant is challenging finding regarding liability.
He has also seeking for enhancement of compensation.

Hence, points that arise for consideration are:
"1. Whether finding of tribunal regarding liability of insurer calls for interference ?
2. Whether claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for?"
13. Insofar as liability, on perusal of Ex.P7- Notarized copy of R.C extract of vehicle in question, it is seen that gross vehicle weight is mentioned as 11,900 k.gs.
Ex.P6-Notarized copy of driving licence would indicate that driver was authorized to drive light motor vehicle.

Since vehicle in question was in excess of 7,500 k.g's in gross vehicle weight, claimant would not be entitled for benefit of ratio as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Mukund Dewangan Vs Oriental Insurance Company Raju S/O Govindappa vs Sateesh S/O Panduranga Rajpure on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68318192/

sentences.text:
Limited reported in (2017) 14 Supreme Court Cases 663.
14.
At same time, claimant in question is third party and there is no material to indicate that accident occurred only on account of lack of driving licence.
Under circumstances, tribunal would not be justified in absolving insurer from liability.

In peculiar facts and circumstances of case, it would be appropriate to direct insurer to pay compensation to claimant first and thereafter recover it from owner without recourse to separate proceedings.
Point no.1 for consideration is answered partly in affirmative as above.

POINT NO.2:
15.
Insofar as quantum of compensation, claimant was aged 22 years working as JCB operator and earning Rs.8,000/- per month.
But same was not substantiated with evidence.
In absence, tribunal would be justified in assessing it notionally.
Notional income for year 2009 is Rs.5,000/- as per norms adopted by Karnataka State Legal Services Committee for settlement of cases before Lok-Adalath.
Therefore, tribunal would not be justified in taking it at Rs.3,000/-.
It has to be considered at Rs.5,000/-.

16. Considering loss of earning capacity at 10% as assessed by tribunal, which appears to be just and proper, future loss of income would require re-assessment as follows:
'Rs.5,000/- X 10% X 12 X 18 = Rs.1,08,000/-'
17.
Considering fact that claimant had sustained fracture of patella, award of Rs.12,000/- towards pain and suffering would be inadequate.
It is enhanced to Rs.20,000/-.
18. Normally fractures take about three months to heal.
Therefore, claimant would be entitled for award of loss of income during layoff period at Rs.15,000/-.
19. Tribunal has not awarded any compensation towards loss of amenities.
It is deemed fit to grant sum of Rs.15,000/- towards same.
20. Tribunal has awarded Rs.2,000/- each towards medical expenses and other incidental expenses.

Taking into account fact that claimant - 10 - has not produced any medical bills and taking inpatient period is for five days, it would be appropriate to award lump-sum compensation of Rs.10,000/- towards medical and other incidental expenses.

Thus, claimant is entitled for reassessed compensation as follows:-
Sl.no.

Heads Amount  (in Rs.)
1. Pain and suffering 20,000/-
Raju S

2. Medical and other 10,000/-
 incidental charges 3. Loss of amenities 15,000/-
4. Loss of income during laid 15,000/-
 up period 5. Future loss of income 1,08,000/-
 Total: Rs.1,68,000/-
Therefore, point for consideration is answered partly in affirmative as above.

21. Hence following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed in part.
- 11 - ii.
Claimant is held entitled for reassessed compensation of Rs.1,68,000/- as against Rs.86,800/- awarded by tribunal, which shall carry interest at 6% per annum from date of claim petition till deposit.
iii. Insurer is directed to pay compensation to claimant and thereafter recover same from owner without recourse to separate proceedings.
iv. Insurer is directed to deposit balance compensation within six weeks.

v. On deposit, tribunal is directed to keep Rs.50,000/- in fixed deposit initially for a period of three years and release remaining amount with proportionate interest in favour of claimant on proper identification.
Claimant is at liberty to withdraw periodical interest on deposit.
